caption.text:
Christian Dior’s Junon dress (Fall/ Winter 1949) is one of couture’s most iconic creations.

Its skirt, made entirely of ombré silk-tulle petals arranged like peacock feathers, references Juno, the Roman goddess.

Each petal was hand-shaped, dyed, and beaded by Maison Rébé, while the bodice features intricate sequin embroidery.

The original gown is preserved at The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Dior recreated a modern version for Natalie Portman at Cannes 2023, but many feel it didn’t capture the original’s breathtaking drama.

✍️: @archivedrunway

this archival footage was first shared by @deadblossoms
